//: 'Mu-jump' / 'transition' braking — drive onto ice while braking.
//1: Standard automotive validation test: accelerate on dry asphalt,
//2: settle, begin braking while still on asphalt, then cross onto ice
//3: at speed.  Exercises ABS adaptation as the friction limit drops
//6: Without ABS the wheels stay locked into the ice transition; the
//7: car slides until friction alone stops it.  With ABS the wheels
//8: back off to peak slip on ice and the car decelerates roughly at
//11: THE TRANSITION BELONGS INSIDE THE BRAKE EVENT, NOT INSIDE THE
//12: LAUNCH.  It used to be inside the launch: the runway was 40 m, and
//13: the pre-brake half of this scenario needs 112 m of it (43.8 m to
//14: reach 15 m/s, then 63.3 m of settle, then 4.9 m of braking).  So
//15: the car crossed onto the ice at full throttle and braking began
//17: mu-jump this scenario exists for never happened, and what actually
//18: ran was a duplicate of abs_low_mu_stop on a slicker surface.  The
//19: runway now covers the whole pre-brake half (see
//20: level/flat_ice_transition.json for the distance budget): entry speed
//21: and a 4.28 s / 63.3 m settle both land on asphalt, the brake goes
//22: on with the car settled and still on asphalt at 14.29 m/s, and the
//23: boundary is 4.9 m later — 42 % of the 11.6 m an asphalt stop from
//24: that speed takes at the surface's own friction limit, so the
//25: crossing happens under braking at >= 10.9 m/s (24 mph) no matter
//26: how well ABS performs.  Measured with no BTCM attached: crosses at
//27: 13.69 m/s (30.6 mph), 0.36 s after the brake goes on.
//29: The brake application is unchanged — same full 1.0, same 19 s hold.
//30: Every event from the brake onward is shifted +6 s so it sits after
//31: the settle instead of firing the instant the wait_for_speed barrier
//32: releases (which is what a 6.0 s brake behind an 8-10 s barrier
//33: actually did: zero settle, throttle release and full brake on the
//37: asphalt for the first 200 m, then ice for 500 m).
